# The four-phase skeleton (the contract every cookbook obeys)

This is the single source of truth for the *shape* of every workflow this skill
produces. A cookbook fills in language-specific commands; it must never change
the structure described here. If a cookbook and this document disagree, this
document wins.

## The job

Every generated `ci.yml` is a single workflow with one job (`ci`) on
`ubuntu-latest`, triggered three ways, with the permissions the Push phase needs:

```yaml
# Generated by ci-bootstrap. Review before merging.
name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches:
    - __DEFAULT_BRANCH__      # push-phase + main-branch analysis
  pull_request:               # build/test/sonar on every PR
  workflow_dispatch:          # allow manual runs
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write             # needed to push the image to GHCR
jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # ── setup (cookbook) ──
      # ── Build (cookbook) ──
      # ── Test (cookbook) ──
      # ── Sonar (cookbook, wrapped in the Sonar guard) ──
      # ── Push (fixed: Dockerfile + GHCR login + build/push) ──
```

## The four phases, in order

Every workflow has exactly these, each as steps whose **names contain the phase
word** (this is how the phase is recognised):

1. **Build** — one step named `Build`. Installs deps / compiles. Cookbook supplies the command(s).
2. **Test** — one step named `Test`. Runs the tests. Cookbook supplies the command(s).
3. **Sonar** — one or more steps whose names contain `Sonar`. Cookbook supplies the scanner invocation.
4. **Push** — the fixed steps below. Cookbook supplies only the default Dockerfile.

## The two guards (fixed, not configurable)

Both guards exist so the workflow does **not** spuriously fail before the repo
has wired up its secrets/registry. They are always present.

**Sonar guard** — every Sonar step carries:

```yaml
    if: ${{ env.SONAR_TOKEN != '' }}
    env:
      SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
      GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

So the scan runs only once a `SONAR_TOKEN` secret is set; otherwise it is
skipped, green.

**Push guard** — every Push step carries `if: github.event_name == 'push'`, so
the image is built and pushed only on a push to the default branch, never on a
pull request.

## The Push phase (identical in every cookbook)

Only the Dockerfile heredoc differs per language; everything else is fixed. The
Dockerfile step is included so a repo with no `Dockerfile` still gets one; if the
repo already has a `Dockerfile`, omit that first step.

```yaml
      - name: Write default Dockerfile (Push)
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          cat > Dockerfile <<'DOCKERFILE'
          __COOKBOOK_DEFAULT_DOCKERFILE__
          DOCKERFILE
      - name: Log in to GHCR (Push)
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Build and push image (Push)
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ github.sha }}
```

## Placeholders filled at generation time

Cookbooks use these tokens; substitute them when writing the final file:

| Placeholder | Replace with | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `__DEFAULT_BRANCH__` | the repo's default branch (e.g. `main`) | scope push-branch triggers |
| `__SONAR_ORG__` | repo **owner, lowercased** | SonarCloud lowercases GitHub-imported org keys |
| `__SONAR_PROJECT_KEY__` | `<owner>_<name>` (owner's original case) | SonarCloud project-key convention |

## Checklist for writing a new cookbook

A new cookbook is a complete `ci.yml` that:

- [ ] keeps the `name`/`on`/`permissions`/`jobs.ci` header verbatim (only
      `__DEFAULT_BRANCH__` varies);
- [ ] has a `Checkout` step, then toolchain **setup** step(s) for the language;
- [ ] has exactly one `Build` step and one `Test` step, using that stack's real commands;
- [ ] has Sonar step(s) named with `Sonar`, each carrying the **Sonar guard** above,
      invoking the scanner appropriate to the stack;
- [ ] ends with the **Push phase** exactly as above, changing only the Dockerfile heredoc;
- [ ] uses `__SONAR_ORG__` / `__SONAR_PROJECT_KEY__` so the project wiring is filled in per-repo.

If all boxes are checked, the workflow is consistent with every other cookbook
and needs no changes to SKILL.md.
